questions.question: You have a five-dollar bill, 1 quarter, and 2 dimes. How much is that?
questions.explain: Add the cents together: 25 plus 10 plus 10 is 45 cents. The trap is adding 25 again for the dime, like you are still counting quarters.

questions.question: You have a ten-dollar bill, 1 dime, and 1 quarter. How much is that?
questions.explain: The dime is 10 and the quarter is 25, so the cents add to 35. Be careful not to keep adding 10 after you switch to the quarter.

questions.question: Mia earned some money at a bake sale. She got a ten-dollar bill, 2 quarters, and 1 nickel. How much did she earn?
questions.explain: Count the cents first: 25 plus 25 plus 5 is 55 cents. The trap is adding 25 for the nickel, as if it were another quarter.

questions.question: At the market, Leo paid the seller. She counted his money: a twenty-dollar bill, 1 quarter, and 3 nickels. How much did Leo pay?
questions.explain: The quarter is 25 and the three nickels add 15, making 40 cents. Be careful not to keep adding 25 after you switch to nickels.

questions.question: You have a five-dollar bill, 2 quarters, and 1 dime. Which is the right way to count it?
options: Start with the dollars, then add the cents
Add the bill and the cents as one number
Count the pieces, not what each is worth
Keep adding the quarter value for every coin
questions.explain: Keep the dollars in their own group and the cents in another, then combine them at the end. The trap is adding 5 and 60 as if they were the same kind of number.

questions.question: Ben starts with a ten-dollar bill and 1 nickel. He earns 3 dimes helping his mom. How much does he have now?
questions.explain: After the nickel (5 cents), add 10 for each dime: 5 plus 10 plus 10 plus 10 is 35 cents. Do not add 5 for the dimes, because a dime is worth 10, not 5.

questions.question: You have a five-dollar bill, 1 quarter, and some dimes. The total is 5 dollars and 75 cents. How many dimes do you have?
questions.explain: Subtract the quarter from 75: 75 minus 25 is 50, and 50 divided by 10 gives 5 dimes. The trap is adding 25 three times and saying 2 dimes.

questions.question: Tom counts a five-dollar bill, 2 quarters, and 1 dime. He says: 5, 25, 50, 75. What did Tom do wrong?
options: He added the bill and cents as one number
He counted pieces instead of adding values
He started with 10 instead of with 5
He added 25 for the dime instead of 10
questions.explain: After 50, a dime adds 10 to make 60, not 25 to make 75. The trap is keeping the old step (adding 25) after you switch to a smaller coin.

questions.question: Here is a group of money: one five-dollar bill, 1 quarter, and 2 nickels. How much is the group worth?
questions.explain: Say the bill first, then count the coins: 5 dollars, then 25, 30, 35 cents. After the quarter you must switch to counting by 5 for each nickel.

questions.question: Look at this group of money: one ten-dollar bill, 3 dimes, and 2 nickels. How much is the group worth?
questions.explain: Count dimes by 10 and nickels by 5: 10, 20, 30, 35, 40 cents. With the bill that is 10 dollars and 40 cents, not 40 coins or 40 alone.

questions.question: A group of money has one twenty-dollar bill, 3 dimes, and 1 quarter. How much is the group worth?
questions.explain: The three dimes make 30 cents, then the quarter adds 25 to make 55 cents. A quarter is worth 25, so do not keep jumping by 10.

questions.question: This group of money has 2 five-dollar bills, 1 quarter, and 1 nickel. How much is in the group?
questions.explain: Two five-dollar bills make 10 dollars, then count 25 and 30 cents. The nickel adds only 5 cents, not another 25.

questions.question: Noah sells lemonade on his street. A neighbour pays him with one ten-dollar bill, 2 dimes, and 2 quarters. How much did Noah earn?
questions.explain: Count the dimes by 10, then each quarter by 25: 10, 20, 45, 70 cents. Dollars and cents stay apart, so he earned 10 dollars and 70 cents.

questions.question: Maya helps at a farm stand on Saturday. She is paid with one twenty-dollar bill, one five-dollar bill, 2 dimes, and 1 nickel. How much was Maya paid?
questions.explain: Add the bills to get 25 dollars, then count 10, 20, 25 cents. The nickel adds 5 cents, so the last jump is small.

questions.question: Jack has one ten-dollar bill, 3 dimes, and 1 nickel. Which is the right way to count his money?
questions.explain: Start with the bill, then count dimes by 10 and the nickel by 5: 10 dollars, then 10, 20, 30, 35 cents. The bill is dollars, so it never joins the cents count.

questions.question: Priya buys berries at the farmers market. She pays with one five-dollar bill, 2 nickels, and 2 quarters. How much did Priya pay?
questions.explain: The two nickels make 10 cents, then each quarter adds 25: 35, 60 cents. So she paid 5 dollars and 60 cents.

questions.question: Jade has one five-dollar bill and 2 nickels. Her brother has 3 dimes. They put all their money together. How much do they have?
questions.explain: Two nickels make 10 cents, and three dimes add 30 more, so the coins are 40 cents. With the bill that is 5 dollars and 40 cents.

questions.question: Ella has one twenty-dollar bill, 3 dimes, and some nickels. Altogether she has 20 dollars and 50 cents. How many nickels does Ella have?
questions.explain: The dimes make 30 cents, so the nickels must make 20 more cents. Count on by 5: 35, 40, 45, 50 — that is 4 nickels.

questions.question: Ravi rakes leaves for two neighbours. On Saturday he earns one five-dollar bill and 2 quarters. On Sunday he earns one ten-dollar bill and 1 dime. How much did Ravi earn in all?
questions.explain: Add the bills first: 5 and 10 make 15 dollars. Then count the coins: 25, 50, 60 cents, because the dime adds only 10.

questions.question: Sam counts one twenty-dollar bill, 2 dimes, and 3 nickels. He says: 20 dollars, then 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 cents. What did Sam do wrong?
options: He counted the coins instead of their values.
He said the bill before counting the coins.
He counted the twenty-dollar bill as 20 cents.
He kept counting by 10 after the dimes.
questions.explain: Nickels are worth 5 cents, so after 20 cents he should say 25, 30, 35. The money is 20 dollars and 35 cents.
